findings.title: When exact alarms are not allowed, the widget/notification refresh fallback calls setAlarmClock, which always throws. No refresh alarm gets set (same code in NotificationUpdater.kt:91-93).
findings.scenario: Setup: an Android 12/12L phone (API 31-32) where the user turned off 'Alarms & reminders' for Vaktinde and did not accept the battery-optimization exemption. Only API 31-32 is affected, because on 13+ the declared USE_EXACT_ALARM is always granted for targetSdk 36. In this state canScheduleExactAlarms() returns false, so setExactAlarm (lines 154-160) and NotificationUpdater.scheduleNextUpdate (lines 91-93) both fall back to setAlarmClock. In AOSP AlarmManagerService.set(), an alarmClock request forces windowLength=0, which makes it exact, so it needs the permission. Without the permission and without the power-allowlist exemption it throws SecurityException('needs to hold SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM or USE_EXACT_ALARM'). That is exactly the case in which canScheduleExactAlarms() returned false, so the fallback can never succeed. Both try/catch blocks swallow the exception, so none of the three providers and not NotificationUpdater get an alarm. Effect after the next prayer time: the always-on notification 888 keeps the old prayer name and its countdown Chronometer runs negative. This lasts until the app is opened or the 6-hour WorkManager task runs. Widgets stay stale until the new 30-minute updatePeriodMillis fires, which can be later in Doze. Part A's Dart code (NotificationService.scheduleModeFor) already handles this same state with inexactAllowWhileIdle, so the native surfaces are the only part still broken in it. The behavior predates this diff but is consolidated here with the comment 'İzin verilmemişse (Android 12) AlarmClockInfo'. The ktrobo exact=false tests pass only because Robolectric's ShadowAlarmManager does not enforce this check. Everything else in this lens checks out. The Kotlin compiles against API 36 (13 unit tests and 80 Robolectric tests pass on identical sources). aapt2 compile/link succeeds. All 16 string keys exist in all 5 locales with no unescaped apostrophes. The TIME_SET/TIMEZONE_CHANGED filters are allowed for manifest receivers and cannot be spoofed by other apps (protected broadcasts). The PendingIntent identities (requestCode 0 per provider class, FLAG_NO_CREATE|FLAG_IMMUTABLE cancel) match. The rollover and after-Yatsı logic is correct. Removing showWhenLocked/turnScreenOn is safe because no fullScreenIntent is used.
findings.fix: In PrayerWidgetData.setExactAlarm, replace the setAlarmClock(AlarmClockInfo(...)) branch with alarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle(AlarmManager.RTC_WAKEUP, targetTime, pendingIntent). It needs no permission and may fire a few minutes late. Make the same change in NotificationUpdater.scheduleNextUpdate, or have it call a shared PrayerWidgetData helper so the logic does not drift again.

findings.title: In inexact mode, any reschedule cancels late ezans/reminders that are due but not yet delivered
findings.scenario: This only affects Android 12/12L with 'Alarms & reminders' turned off. The diff's fallback then schedules everything with inexactAllowWhileIdle. AOSP maxTriggerTime gives these alarms a window of min(0.75 x lead time, 1 h), and Android 12+ LazyAlarmStore only delivers wakeup alarms when some wakeup deadline is reached. So a 13:00 Öğle ezan (ID 4) can still be waiting at 13:05. The plugin removes an entry from its cache only in ScheduledNotificationReceiver.onReceive, so pendingNotificationRequests() still lists ID 4. Any reschedule in that window then drops it. Example: the user opens the app (cold start → _initialize → _rescheduleAlarms). buildAlarmPlan leaves the alarm out because of the !vakitDate.isBefore(now) check on line 299, and _cancelUnplanned calls cancel(4). That calls AlarmManager.cancel, so the ezan never comes. Other triggers do the same: a WorkManager permission/date run, AlarmHealth.onChanged right after the user grants permission (the very moment they noticed the ezan was late), toggles, locale change. End reminders work the same way (line 433 plus _cancelUnplanned on line 544). In 1-day mode, and when day-0 IDs are reused after midnight, the late alarm is overwritten with tomorrow's on the same ID. Confirmed with a throwaway test: canScheduleExact=false, pending=[0,2] for today's passed İmsak/Güneş; rescheduleAlarms cancelled [0,2]. CLAUDE.md promises 'gecikebilir ama çalar'; in fact it can silently never ring.
findings.fix: Keep recently due alarms out of the cancel set. Add an optional keepFrom (for example now minus 65 min) to buildAlarmPlan and buildEndReminderPlan, used only in the past-time filters (lines 299, 347, 433). Pass the IDs of that keep plan together with the real plan IDs to _cancelUnplanned. schedulePrayerNotification and scheduleEndReminder already return early for past times, so the late alarm is neither rescheduled nor cancelled. Apply this at least when NotificationService scheduleModeFor(_exactAllowed) is inexact.

findings.title: Inexact fallback: 'X dakika kaldı' reminders and sahur-end notices can arrive after the event; the banner says only 'a few minutes'
findings.scenario: On Android 12/12L with the permission off, every pre-reminder (odd IDs, for example 'İmsak vaktine 30 dakika kaldı') and every end reminder ('...çıkmasına 15 dakika kaldı') becomes an inexact alarm. These are usually scheduled hours ahead, so AOSP allows up to 1 h late; Android 12+ docs say 'within one hour'. Lazy batching delivers them at the earliest wakeup deadline, which overnight can be close to that hour. Example in Ramadan: the 04:30 sahur reminder arrives at about 05:15, after a 05:00 imsak, still saying 30 minutes are left. The imsak 'Sahur vakti sona erdi' ezan can also be very late. The user may keep eating past imsak. The exactAlarmsOff banner (app_tr.arb:76 'birkaç dakika gecikebilir', and en/de/fr/ar likewise) tells the user the delay is minor, which discourages granting the permission.
findings.fix: When scheduleModeFor(...) is inexact, either skip relative-time reminders (odd IDs and 100–124) or give them absolute-time text (for example 'İmsak 05:00'). Also reword alarmHealthExactOff in all 5 ARBs to say the delay can be up to an hour, and mention imsak/sahur.

findings.title: 'Sessiz modda da çal' does nothing on Android 7.x (minSdk 24) but promises alarm-volume playback
findings.scenario: The tile appears on every API level and says 'Ezan, telefon sessizdeyken de alarm ses seviyesinde çalar'. The alarm stream is applied only through the channel: setupNotificationChannel → NotificationChannel.setSound(uri, AudioAttributes(usage)), which exists on O+ only. On API 24/25 the plugin's setSound() calls NotificationCompat.Builder.setSound(uri), which uses the default notification usage and ignores audioAttributesUsage. On an Android 7 phone in silent/vibrate mode with the toggle on, the ezan stays silent even though the UI says it will ring.
findings.fix: Hide or disable _AlarmStreamTile below SDK 26, for example by checking the SDK version through an existing platform channel or package. Otherwise, add a note in the subtitle that it needs Android 8+.

findings.title: A restored pre-guard backup is 'adopted' (stale device flags kept permanently) when Play updated the app before its first launch on the new phone
findings.scenario: The old phone ran a version without InstallGuard, so its Auto Backup or device-to-device data has permissions_primed=true, battery_optimization_asked=true, alarms_scheduled_date=<old day> and no install_marker. On the new phone (Android 13+, e.g. Honor), Play installs the current build at T0, so firstInstallTime = lastUpdateTime = T0. I checked package_info_plus 9.0.1: installTime/updateTime are PackageInfo.firstInstallTime/lastUpdateTime. Nothing runs before the first launch: WorkManager 2.11 keeps its DB in no_backup and the package is still stopped. If Play auto-updates the app at T1 before that first launch (any install session moves lastUpdateTime), decide(marker:null, hasDeviceFlags:true, updateTime:T1>T0) returns adopted. run() then writes marker=T0, so every later launch is sameInstall and the reset can never happen. Effects: permissions_primed stays true, so primePermissionsIfNeeded returns and the priming/notification/location flow never runs. battery_optimization_asked stays true, so requestBatteryOptimizationOnce never asks for the exemption on the new phone; Honor/Huawei battery management can then delay or kill ezan alarms and the 6-hour WorkManager refresh. If the old phone was Android 12 or lower, POST_NOTIFICATIONS was never granted on the new one, so ezan stays silent until the user notices the AlarmHealth banner and taps it. The window is narrow (only pre-guard backups plus an update before first open), but once it happens the wrong state is permanent.
findings.fix: Before the updateTime heuristic, detect data that is older than this install. Pass the stored 'alarms_scheduled_date' into decide(); this install only ever writes today's date there, so on the same install it can never be earlier than the install day. Return InstallCheck.restored when it is: e.g. `if (alarmsDate != null && alarmsDate.isBefore(DateUtils.dateOnly(DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(installTime)))) return InstallCheck.restored;`. Keep `updateTime > installTime → adopted` only as the fallback when no such date exists, and add a decide() table case for it.

findings.title: The exact-alarm warning says 'a few minutes late', but on Android 12 the fallback alarm can be up to about an hour late
findings.scenario: An Android 12/12L user turns off 'Alarms & reminders' for the app. On the next reschedule, rescheduleAlarms/refreshExactAlarmPermission sets _exactAllowed=false, so scheduleModeFor(false) returns inexactAllowWhileIdle (notification_service.dart:31-34, and the fallback at :165). FLN maps that mode to AlarmManagerCompat.setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP) with a heuristic window. In the Android 12 AlarmManagerService source, maxTriggerTime gives a window of min(75% of the lead time, INTERVAL_HOUR). Ezans are planned up to 5 days ahead, so each one gets a full 60-minute window. LAZY_BATCHING is on by default (DEFAULT_LAZY_BATCHING = true), and LazyAlarmStore sets the wake-up for wake-up alarms at getMaxWhenElapsed(). Its removePendingAlarms only sends them when some wake-up alarm reaches its deadline. On a sleeping phone (yatsı, imsak/sahur) the ezan can therefore arrive close to T+60 min. The banner (alarmHealthExactOff, same text in the en/de/fr/ar ARBs at line 55) tells the user the delay is only 'a few minutes', so they have little reason to tap 'İzin ver'. Before this range these users got no alarm at all, so the fallback is still an improvement. The problem is that the warning understates the delay, and an imsak/iftar alert can be up to an hour late.
findings.fix: Change alarmHealthExactOff in all 5 ARBs to state the real impact (for example 'Alarm izni kapalı: ezan 1 saate kadar gecikebilir, izin verin'), then run flutter gen-l10n. Update the CLAUDE.md note 'gecikebilir ama çalar' to say 'up to ~1 hour'. No code change is needed, because FLN has no setWindow API.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute the claim and couldn't. I checked the Android 12/12L AlarmManagerService and AlarmManager sources (android12-release, android12L-release, 12.0.0_r34 and 12.1.0_r27 are byte-identical).

Why the fallback always fails:
- In set(), an AlarmClockInfo request forces windowLength=0, so it counts as exact.
- REQUIRE_EXACT_ALARM_PERMISSION applies from targetSdk S, and this app targets 36, so the change is on and needsPermission = exact.
- If the app has neither the permission (hasScheduleExactAlarmInternal) nor the power-allowlist exemption (isExemptFromExactAlarmPermission), set() throws SecurityException. DEFAULT_CRASH_NON_CLOCK_APPS is true, so it throws rather than only logging.
- canScheduleExactAlarms() returns true when the change is off, when the app is exempt, or when it holds the permission, and false otherwise. So whenever it returns false, the setAlarmClock fallback must throw.
- The setAlarmClock javadoc and @RequiresPermission(SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM) say the same.
- Both call sites catch the exception and swallow it: scheduleWidgetUpdate's try/catch, and scheduleNextUpdate in NotificationUpdater.kt lines 91-93. As a result, no refresh alarm is set for the three providers or for notification 888.

Who can reach this state:
- The manifest declares SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM with maxSdkVersion=32, so on API 31-32 the app is listed under Settings > Special app access > Alarms & reminders. Users can turn it off there.
- Turning it off also makes the system delete the app's existing exact alarms (removeExactAlarmsOnPermissionRevokedLocked).
- On 13+, the declared USE_EXACT_ALARM permission makes canScheduleExactAlarms() return true, so only Android 12/12L is affected.
- Users who accepted the battery-optimization exemption are also exempt, so the case needs: Android 12/12L, the user turned the permission off, and the exemption declined.
- The app treats this as a supported state. NotificationService.scheduleModeFor falls back to inexactAllowWhileIdle, and alarm_health.dart shows a warning with a fix button. A user who ignores that warning stays in this state.

What the user sees:
- Nothing else refreshes notification 888 periodically. The background service only triggers NotificationUpdater once, at start. The system's APPWIDGET_UPDATE broadcast is sent directly to provider components, and NotificationUpdater is not a provider.
- After each prayer time, the notification keeps the old prayer name. Its Chronometer is a countDown with started=true, so it shows a negative value. This lasts until the app is opened or the 6-hour WorkManager task runs.
- Widgets go stale the same way until the inexact 30-minute updatePeriodMillis fires.

Limits:
- Robolectric's ShadowAlarmManager does not enforce this check, which is why the tests with exact=false pass.
- The impact is cosmetic (no wrong azan; those alarms are set by the Dart side) and needs a rare configuration, so low severity is right.
- The bug is older than this diff.

I reproduced this against the real Android 12 system code, not only by reading it.

1. **App code path.** `PrayerWidgetData.setExactAlarm` (PrayerWidgetData.kt:154-160) and `NotificationUpdater.scheduleNextUpdate` (NotificationUpdater.kt:91-93) call `setAlarmClock` only when `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is false. Both calls sit inside `try/catch(Exception)` that only prints the stack trace.

2. **Android 12 system code.** I disassembled `AlarmManagerService` from the Robolectric android-all 12 jar (SP1A.211105.001, API 31), which includes the server classes.
   - The binder's `canScheduleExactAlarms(pkg)` returns `!changeEnabled || isExemptFromExactAlarmPermission(uid) || hasScheduleExactAlarmInternal(pkg, uid)`.
   - In `set()`, any request with an alarm clock is forced to `windowLength = 0`, so it counts as exact.
   - Compat change 171306433 is on for targetSdk 36, so an exact request needs the permission.
   - When the app has neither the permission nor the exemption, `set()` throws `SecurityException("Caller <pkg> needs to hold android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM to set exact alarms.")`. The flag that controls this, `CRASH_NON_CLOCK_APPS`, defaults to true.
   - That is exactly the condition under which `canScheduleExactAlarms()` returned false, so the fallback can never succeed.

3. **Runtime check.** I wrote a Robolectric test at sdk=31 in a scratch worktree, since removed. It runs the real Android 12 binder `set` and `canScheduleExactAlarms` code; only `setImpl`, the step that stores the alarm, is replaced by a recorder. It drives the app's real `NotificationUpdater` and the three widget providers, built from HEAD.
   - **Revoked, no battery exemption** (exact-alarm app-op set to errored): `canScheduleExactAlarms` returned false 4 times and `setAlarmClock` was called 4 times. Each call threw the `SecurityException` above, the app swallowed it, and 0 alarms were stored. Notification 888 was still posted with a running countdown, so it will go negative after the next prayer time.
   - **Default grant on Android 12:** all 4 used `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle` and all 4 alarms were stored.
   - **Revoked but battery-exempt:** all 4 alarms were stored.
   - **Patched copy using `setAndAllowWhileIdle`, revoked state:** all 4 alarms were stored and no exception was thrown.
   - `setWindow(RTC, …)` also gets past the permission check in the revoked state.

4. **Who is affected.** I checked the Android 13 jar: there `canScheduleExactAlarms` also checks `USE_EXACT_ALARM`, which the manifest declares and Android grants automatically, so the fallback cannot be reached on API 33 and up. Only API 31-32 is affected. On Android 12 the exact-alarm permission is on by default, so the user must have turned off "Alarms & reminders" and also declined the battery-optimization exemption. That is rare but reachable, and the app's Dart side already handles this state with `inexactAllowWhileIdle`.

**Impact.** Cosmetic and it fixes itself:
- **Widgets:** they recover on their 30-minute `updatePeriodMillis` update.
- **Notification 888:** it shows the old prayer name and a countdown below zero until the app is opened, the 6-hour WorkManager task runs, or the clock or time zone changes.

"Low" severity fits.

**Small inaccuracies in the report.**
- The Android 12 error message names only `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`; the "or `USE_EXACT_ALARM`" wording appears from Android 13.
- "A few minutes late" is optimistic. On Android 12 an inexact alarm can fire up to the smaller of 75% of its lead time or 1 hour late. In Doze, Android 12 allows only one inexact "allow while idle" alarm per 9 minutes per app, shared with the Dart prayer alarms that use `inexactAllowWhileIdle`.
- Android 12L (API 32) was not checked directly because no jar was available.

I traced every step and confirmed each one with the Dart code, the plugin source and the Android 12 platform source.

**Who it affects.** The manifest declares SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM only up to API 32 and USE_EXACT_ALARM for newer versions. So `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is false only on Android 12/12L (API 31/32), and only when the user has turned off "Alarms & reminders". The group is a bit narrower than the claim says: in Android 12, `canScheduleExactAlarms()` also returns true when the user exempted the app from battery optimization (`isExemptFromExactAlarmPermission` checks the device-idle allowlist, which includes apps the user exempted). The app asks for that exemption once. Only users who refused it fall back to `inexactAllowWhileIdle`. The app does treat this state as supported (banner, WorkManager re-run on permission change).

**Delay (Android 12 platform source).**
- `setAndAllowWhileIdle` uses the heuristic window: `maxTriggerTime` gives min(0.75 × lead time, 1 h). Ezan alarms are planned 5 days ahead, so the window is effectively 1 hour.
- Lazy batching is on by default. In `LazyAlarmStore.removePendingAlarms`, wakeup alarms are only sent once some wakeup alarm's deadline has passed. Turning the screen on does not flush them.
- So a 13:00 ezan can still be waiting in AlarmManager for up to about an hour.

**Plugin side (flutter_local_notifications 18.0.1).**
- `pendingNotificationRequests` reads the plugin's own cached list. An entry leaves that list only in `ScheduledNotificationReceiver.onReceive` or in `cancel`.
- `cancel` calls `AlarmManager.cancel` on the same PendingIntent, so the alarm is gone.
- `zonedSchedule` with the same ID replaces the existing alarm.

**Dart side, reproduced with a throwaway test** (mocked plugin channel modelling the cache and AlarmManager; inexact mode; TZ Istanbul):
- **5-day mode:** I placed Öğle 3 minutes in the past (longitude 66.55) with ID 4 pending. `rescheduleAlarms` (the cold-start path) called cancel(4). `runHeadless` with a stale `alarms_scheduled_date` did the same.
- **1-day mode:** ID 4 was overwritten with tomorrow's time.
- **End reminders:** ID 120, already due, was cancelled.
- **Extra case the claim does not cover:** if today's alarms were planned yesterday, today's Öğle has ID 16 (numbering from yesterday's run). The first reschedule of the day gives ID 16 to tomorrow's Öğle and overwrites the late one.

**When it happens.** Reopening the app after its screen was closed always reschedules, because MainActivity is a plain FlutterActivity and a new engine runs `_initialize`. People often open a prayer app right around prayer time. Other triggers: alarm toggles and sound changes, AlarmHealth.onChanged when the permission is granted, and WorkManager.

Before commit e406355 everything used alarmClock and fired on time, so this window did not exist. The inexact fallback created it, and it breaks the documented promise "gecikebilir ama çalar" (may be late but will ring).

**Problems with the proposed fix.**
- The keep set uses today's numbering (day 0) only. It misses the 1-day overwrite (the shift to tomorrow on line 295 still lands on the same ID) and the overwrite caused by yesterday's numbering.
- "Only when inexact" misses the AlarmHealth case. Once the user grants the permission the mode becomes exact, but the late alarm was scheduled inexact.
- Keeping late pre-reminders and end reminders has little value: when they arrive late they can say a prayer time is ending after it has already ended.

**Severity.** The defect is real but affects few users. When it hits, the ezan silently never rings.

I tried to refute it and could not. Each link in the chain checks out.

1. **What the plugin does (flutter_local_notifications 18.0.1).** `inexactAllowWhileIdle` becomes `AlarmManagerCompat.setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP)`. `pendingNotificationRequests()` only reads the plugin's SharedPreferences cache. An entry leaves that cache only in two places: in `ScheduledNotificationReceiver.onReceive` (via `scheduleNextNotification` → `removeNotificationFromCache`), or when `cancel()` is called. `cancel()` calls `AlarmManager.cancel(pendingIntent)`, so an alarm that has not been delivered yet is destroyed.

2. **What Android 12/12L does (AOSP android12-release source, fetched).**
   - `setAndAllowWhileIdle` uses `WINDOW_HEURISTIC`, so `maxTriggerTime` = min(trigger + 0.75 × lead time, trigger + 1 h).
   - `DEFAULT_LAZY_BATCHING` is true, so `LazyAlarmStore` is used. Its `removePendingAlarms` sends wakeup alarms only when some wakeup alarm reaches its deadline. Turning the screen on does not flush them.
   - So delivery minutes, or up to 1 h, after the nominal time is normal. The Android docs also say inexact alarms fire "within one hour".

3. **What the app does.**
   - `buildAlarmPlan` drops past times (line 299).
   - `_cancelUnplanned` (line 657) cancels every pending ID in 0-59 that is not in the plan.
   - End reminders behave the same way (line 433 and line 544).
   - I ran a probe test in a temporary worktree (since removed): `canScheduleExact=false`, `pending=[0,2]` after İmsak and Güneş. `rescheduleAlarms` called `cancel` for [0, 2], in `inexactAllowWhileIdle` mode.

4. **The reschedule triggers are routine.**
   - Every UI cold start: `_initialize` → `_rescheduleAlarms`. `MainActivity` is a plain `FlutterActivity`.
   - The first WorkManager run of the day.
   - `AlarmHealth.onChanged` after the permission is granted from the banner.
   - Alarm toggles, sound changes and locale changes.

   A natural sequence for an affected user: the ezan is late, the user opens the app to check, and the ezan never rings.

**Who is affected.** The manifest declares `USE_EXACT_ALARM`, and in AOSP 13 `canScheduleExactAlarms` returns true when an app holds it. `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` has `maxSdkVersion` 32. So only Android 12/12L users who turned off "Alarms & reminders" are affected; the permission is granted by default. That is a narrow group, and the failure is probabilistic. But it is exactly the state that the new inexact fallback and the health banner were built for, and the code claims "gecikebilir ama çalar". The mechanism is certain; how often it happens in practice is not. That uncertainty is why confidence is medium rather than high.
verdicts.refinedFix:
**Idea:** do not cancel alarms whose time passed less than about 65 minutes ago. On Android 12/12L an inexact alarm can still be waiting in AlarmManager for up to 1 hour after its time.

**1. Add a cutoff parameter to both plan builders.** In `PrayerRefreshService.buildAlarmPlan` and `buildEndReminderPlan`, add an optional `DateTime? keepFrom` and compute `final cutoff = keepFrom ?? now;`.
- Use `cutoff` only in the "already past" checks:
  - line 295: the 1-day shift → `vakitDate.isBefore(cutoff)`
  - line 299: `!vakitDate.isBefore(cutoff)`
  - line 347: `hatirlatmaZamani.isAfter(cutoff)`
  - line 433: `!remindAt.isAfter(cutoff)`
- Day and ID math (`dayDate`, `PrayerTracker.addDays`) keeps using `now`.

**2. Change `rescheduleAlarms` and `_syncEndReminders`.**
- Build the plan with `keepFrom: now.subtract(const Duration(minutes: 65))`.
- Pass all of that plan's IDs to `_cancelUnplanned`. A recently due alarm that has not been delivered then stays pending and is neither cancelled nor overwritten.
- Schedule and count only `plan.where((a) => !a.time.isBefore(now))`. `schedule*()` already returns early for past times; filtering keeps `succeeded` accurate.

**Edge cases:**
- This is harmless in exact mode, because delivered alarms are no longer in the plugin cache. So it can be applied always, or only when `NotificationService.scheduleModeFor(_exactAllowed)` is inexact.
- A user who turns a vakit off, or presses "Kıldım" for an end reminder, still gets it cancelled, because it drops out of the plan.
- Not covered: day-index ezan IDs being reused after midnight (a late Yatsı past 00:00 at high latitudes). That would need date-stable IDs (epochDay % 5, as end reminders already use).

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced this through the app, the plugin and the Android 12 platform source.

Which users can hit it:
- The manifest declares `USE_EXACT_ALARM` and `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` (maxSdkVersion 32). So `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is always true on Android 13+.
- It can only be false on Android 12/12L (API 31/32), when the user has turned off "Alarms & reminders" for the app.
- Android 12's `canScheduleExactAlarms()` also returns true for apps on the battery-optimization allowlist. The app's `requestBatteryOptimizationOnce` cannot make the app exempt: `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` is not in the app manifest or any plugin manifest, so `permission_handler` returns "denied" without showing a dialog.
- So the affected group is small but real. The app already has a fallback and a banner written for exactly this group.

Code path:
- `rescheduleAlarms` and `syncEndReminders` call `refreshExactAlarmPermission()`, which sets `_exactAllowed = false`.
- `_zonedSchedule` then uses `scheduleModeFor(false)`, which is `inexactAllowWhileIdle`.
- The plugin (flutter_local_notifications 18.0.1, `setupAllowWhileIdleAlarm`) turns that into `AlarmManagerCompat.setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP, ...)`.
- When the alarm fires, `ScheduledNotificationReceiver.onReceive` shows the notification with its stored text however late it is.

Android 12 platform source (android12-release, GitHub mirror):
